items.question: Which world-groups are assigned to niyati, kāla, rāga, and the vidyā-kalā pair?
premises: In niyati there is a group of ten Śaṅkaras.
In kāla there is a group of ten Śivas, forming a pair of cities.
In rāga there is the well-delighted world and the teacher-disciple city.
In the pair of vidyā and kalā further worlds are assigned.
items.inference: The tattvas niyati, kāla, rāga, and the vidyā-kalā pair each contain specific named world-groups in the spatial hierarchy.
uncertainties: The exact identity of the ten Śaṅkaras and ten Śivas is not specified in this verse.
items.plain_english: In the tattva of restriction there are ten Śaṅkara worlds; in time there are ten Śiva worlds, making two cities. In attachment there are the well-delighted world and the teacher-disciple city, and in the pair of knowledge and limited agency there are further worlds.

items.question: How many cities belong to vidyā together with the seven tattvas beginning with puruṣa?
premises: World after world is placed in night, including the three cities of the sheath.
The city of speech and the city of measure are included.
Vidyā, joined with the seven tattvas beginning with puruṣa, has twenty-seven cities.
items.inference: The domain of vidyā together with the seven tattvas beginning with puruṣa comprises twenty-seven worlds in total.
uncertainties: The sense of 'niśi' (in night) as a cosmological division is not fully clear from this verse alone.
items.plain_english: World after world is set out, including the three sheath-cities, the city of speech, and the city of measure. Thus vidyā, together with the seven tattvas beginning with puruṣa, contains twenty-seven cities.

items.question: Which pure worlds and principles are enumerated in the domain of pure knowledge?
premises: Vāmeśa, Rūpa, and Sūkṣma belong to the pure domain.
Pure knowledge and the measure of Śakti’s radiance are included.
Suviśuddhi, Śiva, Mokṣa, Dhuva, Īśa, Saṃbuddha, Samaya, and Sauśiva are named.
items.inference: The verse enumerates a sequence of pure worlds and principles associated with śuddhavidyā and the higher pure order.
uncertainties: The exact boundaries between tattvas and world-names in this list are compressed in the compound.
items.plain_english: In the pure domain are Vāmeśa, Rūpa, and Sūkṣma; then pure knowledge and the measure of Śakti’s radiance; then Suviśuddhi and Śiva, and the worlds named Mokṣa, Dhuva, Īśa, Saṃbuddha, Samaya, and Sauśiva.

items.question: What constitutes the seventeen-city domain of the peaceful level?
premises: The peaceful level has seventeen cities.
It is joined with the three cities of Vidyeśa and Sadāśiva.
It includes Bindu, Half-moon, and Nirodhikā.
It extends to the supreme Sauśiva and the Indhikā and other cities of the central channel.
items.inference: The śāntā level is defined as a seventeen-world domain spanning Vidyeśa-Sadāśiva cities and subtle principles up to the central-channel Sauśiva region.
uncertainties: The precise parsing of 'indhikādi' as a world-name series is inferred from context.
items.plain_english: The peaceful level has seventeen cities. It includes the three cities of the Vidyeśas and Sadāśiva, the principles Bindu, Half-moon, and Nirodhikā, and reaches up to the supreme Sauśiva and the Indhikā and other cities of the central channel.

items.question: Which five cities follow after the supreme sound and related subtle principles?
premises: The supreme sound, the cavity of Brahman, and the upper Kuṇḍalinī joined with Sūkṣma and others are named.
Śakti is included in this sequence.
Five cities are supported by Vyāpin, Vyoman, Ananta, and Anātha.
items.inference: After the highest subtle principles, five cities are established in dependence on Vyāpin, Vyoman, Ananta, and Anātha.
uncertainties: The syntactic role of 'śaktiḥ' in the list is slightly compressed and may mark a transition.
items.plain_english: There are the supreme sound, the cavity of Brahman, the upper Kuṇḍalinī joined with Sūkṣma and others, and Śakti; then come five cities supported by Vyāpin, Vyoman, Ananta, and Anātha.

items.question: What alternative arrangements are given for the sixth and the Samanā world-group?
premises: A sixth city is supported by Paramamanas.
Alternatively, there is a sixteen-world group of Samanā.
Another arrangement includes the enclosure of Bindu, the supreme Sauśiva, and five worlds beginning with Indhikā.
items.inference: The text presents alternative ways of counting or grouping the highest subtle worlds around Paramamanas, Samanā, Bindu, and Sauśiva.
uncertainties: The exact equivalence between the two alternative groupings is not spelled out in this verse.
items.plain_english: Then there is a sixth, supported by Paramamanas. Alternatively, one may speak of the sixteen-world group of Samanā, or of the enclosure of Bindu, the supreme Sauśiva, and the five worlds beginning with Indhikā.

rows.grounds: highest subtle principle in this set

items.question: How is the sixteen-world group of the beyond-peace level defined?
premises: The central-channel domain, the cavity of Brahman, Kuṇḍalinī, the five Vyāpins, and Samanā are listed.
Together these form a sixteen-world group.
This group is identified with the pair of tattvas of the beyond-peace level.
items.inference: The śāntyatītā level consists of sixteen worlds corresponding to a pair of tattvas and culminating in Samanā.
uncertainties: The exact internal count that yields sixteen from the listed items is not itemized in the verse.
items.plain_english: The central-channel domain, the cavity of Brahman, Kuṇḍalinī, the five Vyāpins, and Samanā together make up this sixteen-world group. This is the pair of tattvas belonging to the level beyond peace.

items.question: What world-order is reported from the Mataṅga scripture at the lowest level?
premises: The revered Mataṅga scripture gives a sequence of world-groups.
That sequence begins with Kālāgni and the hells.
It includes a hundred, principally joined with forty.
items.inference: According to the Mataṅga scripture, the lower cosmological sequence starts from Kālāgni and the hells and is counted as one hundred and forty in its main reckoning.
uncertainties: The exact referent of the additional forty within the hundred is not specified in this verse.
items.plain_english: In the revered Mataṅga scripture this sequence of cities is given: beginning with Kālāgni and the hells, it amounts principally to one hundred and forty.

items.question: What regions make up the middle of the cosmic egg and what lies outside it?
premises: Kūṣmāṇḍa, the seven netherworlds, the seven worlds, and Maheśvara form the middle of the egg.
Outside that middle there are a hundred Rudras.
These Rudras are described as situated there.
items.inference: The cosmic egg’s interior is structured by lower and upper world-series under Maheśvara, while a hundred Rudras occupy the region beyond it.
uncertainties: Whether 'Kūṣmāṇḍa' names a world, a being, or both is not explicit in this verse.
items.plain_english: Kūṣmāṇḍa, the seven netherworlds, the seven worlds, and Maheśvara make up the middle of the cosmic egg. Outside that, a hundred Rudras are situated.

items.question: How are the two hundred and fifty-seven stations distributed in the elemental grouping?
premises: There are two hundred places forming a level.
That level is joined with fifty-seven more.
From the middle of a group of five eights, thirty-two are placed in the four elements.
items.inference: The verse gives a numerical distribution of 257 stations, with thirty-two of them assigned within the four-element grouping derived from a larger set.
uncertainties: The structure of the 'group of five eights' and its relation to the total count is mathematically compressed.
items.plain_english: There is a level of two hundred places joined with fifty-seven more. From the middle of a group of five eights, thirty-two are assigned within the four elements.

items.question: How are groups of five and eight assigned across the subtle elements and inner faculties?
premises: Five are placed in the subtle elements.
The Viśvedevas are there, followed by a group of eight.
A fifth group is associated with the senses, egoity, intellect, and the guṇas, including a group of eight gods.
items.inference: The cosmological count continues by assigning groups of five and eight to the tanmātras and to inner faculties such as senses, egoity, intellect, and guṇa.
uncertainties: The exact mapping of each group to each faculty is compressed and not fully explicit.
items.plain_english: In the subtle elements there are five, and there are the Viśvedevas and then a group of eight. A fifth grouping is connected with the senses, egoity, intellect, and the guṇas, including a group of eight gods.

items.question: Which groups are assigned to the root, time, niyati, and the tattva of attachment?
premises: A group of eight yogas named Krodha is placed in the root.
It is associated with time and with Naiyati.
Patadruga and others, and Aṅguṣṭhamātra and others, belong to the tattva of attachment.
items.inference: The enumeration continues by locating specific named groups in the root, in kāla with niyati, and in the rāga tattva.
uncertainties: The form 'sanaiyate' is metrically compressed; it is read here as association with niyati.
items.plain_english: In the root there is a group of eight yogas called Krodha, associated with time and with niyati. Patadruga and others, and Aṅguṣṭhamātra and others, belong to the tattva of attachment.
